newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso rises on strong foreign inflows.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso rises on strong foreign inflows.

text.p: * Volume rises to $111.2 million from $70 million
The Philippine peso edged up against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday, fortified by strong foreign inflows into the local debt market, traders said.
"Banks holding on to dollars also found it more lucrative to shift to pesos because of rising overnight rates," said one trader.
The peso ended at 26.29 from the previous 26.298.
Traders said the Central Bank bought around $10 million at 26.29.
Volume swelled to $111.2 million from Monday's $70 million. The weighted average reached 26.293 from 26.298.
Traders said they expect small fluctuations in the foreign exchange market for the rest of the week. "My bet is the peso still has room for a little upside," one trader said.
